properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: SSH host key verification disabled in Solana cluster provisioning/network scripts (net/common.sh, colo-provider.sh, ec2-provider.sh, colo-utils.sh, create-solana-user.sh). Every ssh invocation into freshly provisioned nodes accepts any host key and writes known-hosts to /dev/null, so the tunnel authenticates nothing — a real posture control (class 9), changeable here, though scoped to ops tooling rather than shipped validator code.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: sha1@0.10.5 declared in the workspace Cargo.lock — the SHA-1 crate ships in the Rust build graph (dep_scan basis). This is the dependency inventory: the image carries SHA-1 whether or not a first-party call site is visible to the regex. Changeable here by dropping the dependency.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: secp256k1 is a core Solana asset: the libsecp256k1 0.6.0 dependency backs the native secp256k1_recover precompile (programs/sbf/c/src/secp256k1_recover/secp256k1_recover.c, the bpf_loader syscall at programs/bpf_loader/src/syscalls/mod.rs:320, sdk/bpf/c/inc/sol/secp256k1.h) providing ECDSA public-key recovery over secp256k1 for on-chain programs (Ethereum-compatible signing). Classical ECDSA — broken by Shor. Many of the 185 sites are fee/cost-model counters (SECP256K1_VERIFY_COST, num_secp256k1

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: All 70 sites examined: == / != comparisons on public chain data — SHA-256-based Hash values (blockhash, bank/frozen hash, PoH tick hash, genesis hash, snapshot hashes), Ed25519 Signature values (default checks, log lookups), gossip CRDS value_hash and Ping/Pong tokens, shred Merkle/signature equality. A handful of sites (fee_calculator/fee.rs lamports_per_signature) are fee arithmetic, not digests. No secret-dependent comparison observed — the timing-leak posture concern is hygiene-level, since

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Ed25519 is THE signature scheme of this blockchain: every transaction is Ed25519-signed and verified through core/src/sigverify.rs (ed25519_verify / ed25519_verify_cpu, with the GPU path in perf) and the core sigverify stage; gossip CRDS values are signed with node identity Ed25519 keypairs; ed25519-dalek-bip32 provides hierarchical key derivation for wallets. ed25519_verify_disabled (core/src/sigverify_stage.rs:228) is the deliberate skip path used on dev/test deployments. Classical EdDSA — Sho

properties.value: IDENTITY CORRECTION: no X25519 key agreement exists anywhere in this codebase (grep for x25519/X25519 in *.rs: 0 matches). The object's 120 sites are curve25519-dalek — Edwards/Ristretto255 GROUP OPERATIONS, not X25519 key exchange: the curve25519-dalek 3.2.1 dependency (patched to the solana-labs fork, Cargo.toml:543-544), point decompression in perf sigverify (CompressedEdwardsY/Scalar, perf/src/sigverify.rs:689), the curve25519 BPF syscalls (edwards/ristretto validate/add/subtract/multiply/ms

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Genuine ECDSA use in this repo is SSH-key material, not validator code: (1) ci/setup-new-buildkite-agent/setup-buildkite.sh:47 runs ssh-keygen -t ecdsa to mint the buildkite agent's SSH identity; (2) 15 committed ecdsa-sha2-nistp256 public keys in net/scripts/solana-user-authorized_keys.sh authorize Solana staff/CI machines onto cluster nodes. Classical NIST-P256 ECDSA — Shor-vulnerable key material, changeable here by rotating to Ed25519 or PQ SSH keys. The 4 debug!-literal sites were rejected

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The same committed SSH keys as the ECDSA object: 15 ecdsa-sha2-nistp256 (NIST P-256) public keys in net/scripts/solana-user-authorized_keys.sh authorizing Solana staff and buildkite CI machines onto cluster nodes — curve-level view of the same key material. Shor-vulnerable; PQ replacement would be Ed25519 now / PQ SSH later.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: ed25519-dalek@1.0.1 pinned in the workspace Cargo.lock — this is Solana's core signature library: every transaction signature and shred signature on the network is Ed25519 verified through this crate. Shor-vulnerable signature scheme (migration ML-DSA-65/SLH-DSA, a network-wide change, not just a crate bump). Dependency inventory entry; the version pin (1.x, not 2.x) is also worth a reader's attention.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Live protocol configuration in CI bootstrap: curl --tlsv1.2 floors the TLS version for the rustup downloads in ci/docker/Dockerfile:70 and ci/setup-new-buildkite-agent/setup-buildkite.sh:53. A TLS 1.2 minimum admits classical ECDHE key exchange and cannot negotiate hybrid PQ groups (which require 1.3); trivially changeable here to --tlsv1.3.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: curve25519-dalek@3.2.1 declared in Cargo.lock — supplies Curve25519 group arithmetic (Ed25519 signing, X25519 where used) to the Rust build graph. Dependency inventory entry; classical curve arithmetic, Shor-vulnerable. Changeable here by dependency update.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: X25519 via ring@0.16.20 in Cargo.lock — ring is the crypto provider behind this build's TLS path (rustls pulls it in for the RPC/HTTPS layer). X25519 is the harvest-now-decrypt-later KEX; the 0.16 ring line predates any PQ or hybrid group support entirely, so the shipped stack cannot negotiate PQ key exchange without upgrading. Dependency inventory entry, changeable here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: AES-128-GCM-SIV is the authenticated encryption behind Solana's confidential (zk) token balances: zk-token-sdk/src/encryption/auth_encryption.rs encrypts/decrypts ciphertexts with Aes128GcmSiv (encrypt/decrypt at :77/:93), and zk-keygen is the CLI that generates and seed-phrase-recovers the AES128 keys (main.rs KeyType::Aes128 paths; Cargo.toml:8 is the package description of exactly this). AES-128 is Grover-only (64-bit effective security post-quantum, below CNSA 2.0 preference for AES-256); GC

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: AES via node-forge@1.3.1 in the docs npm graph — the symmetric-cipher facet of the same node-forge dependency already inventoried. AES is not Shor-broken (Grover only halves the effective key size); kept for completeness of the dependency inventory. No first-party call site found in docs code.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: sha2@0.9.9 declared in the workspace Cargo.lock — the SHA-256/SHA-512 implementation used across the validator (block hashing, Ed25519 expand, PoH context). SHA-2 is quantum-resistant in practice (Grover gives quadratic speedup only); this entry documents what the build ships. Note sha2 0.9.x is an older line than current 0.10.x.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: ed25519-dalek as crypto provider (class 6): the library object for the Ed25519 implementation this workspace uses at sdk/src/signer/keypair.rs (Keypair type behind every Solana signer), with tests/benches under programs/ed25519-tests and sdk. Same logical asset as the Ed25519-via-ed25519-dalek@1.0.1 object, reached by the library rule rather than the dependency rule.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: node-forge as crypto provider in the docs-site npm graph (docs/package-lock.json) — library-level view of the same dependency as the RSA-via-node-forge@1.3.1 object. Ships RSA/X.509/PBKDF2 primitives to whatever the docs build invokes; no application call site found in first-party docs code.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: selfsigned@2.1.1 in the docs npm graph (docs/package-lock.json) — generates self-signed X.509 certificates, typically for the Docusaurus dev-server HTTPS. Dependency inventory entry for the docs build; a self-signed-cert generator is a PKI-adjacent capability worth listing. Changeable here by dependency update.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: X.509 certificate support via node-forge@1.3.1 in the docs npm graph — the certificate/PKI facet of the same node-forge dependency already inventoried as the RSA object. Library ships X.509 parsing/generation to the docs build; no first-party call site found in docs code.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: openssl@0.10.64 (Rust bindings) declared in the workspace Cargo.lock — the OpenSSL provider behind native-tls and any direct openssl use in the build. As a crypto provider (class 6) its version decides PQ capability: 0.10.64-era OpenSSL 3.x can negotiate hybrid X25519+ML-KEM when the system library and TLS version allow, so this entry is the pivot for any future PQ TLS work. Changeable here by dependency update; underlying system OpenSSL version is environment-determined.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: sha1@0.10.5 as crypto library in the Rust build graph — library-level view of the same dependency as the SHA-1 algorithm object (sha1 crate, collision-broken hash). Whatever pulls it in (transitive dependency) ships SHA-1 to the build; the crate is the reason SHA-1 is available at all. Changeable here by dropping the dependent edge.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: blake3@1.5.0 declared in the workspace Cargo.lock — the BLAKE3 hash implementation used by the validator (accounts hashing / snapshot hash paths rely on blake3 for speed). BLAKE3 is a modern hash, Grover-only quantum exposure; kept as the provider inventory of what the build ships.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: selfsigned@2.1.1 as crypto library in the docs npm graph — library-level view of the same dependency as the X.509-self-signed object; generates self-signed certificates for the docs dev server. Dependency inventory entry.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: hmac@0.8.1 declared in the workspace Cargo.lock — HMAC (keyed MAC built on SHA-2) available to the build graph, an older 0.8 line. HMAC itself is not Shor-broken (Grover-only exposure); dependency inventory entry documenting what the build ships.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: native-tls@0.2.11 declared in the workspace Cargo.lock — the TLS provider used by the validator's RPC/HTTPS layer (wraps system OpenSSL on Linux). As a protocol provider (class 6) this is the layer that must be upgraded before hybrid X25519+ML-KEM groups can be negotiated on RPC connections; 0.2.x delegates cipher/group choice to the system library, so PQ capability is observable here but decided by the environment's OpenSSL.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: curve25519-dalek@3.2.1 as crypto library in the Rust build graph — library-level view of the same dependency as the Curve25519 algorithm object; supplies the group arithmetic behind Ed25519 verification (and any X25519 use) in the validator. Shor-vulnerable curve arithmetic; changeable here by dependency update.
